title: Polynomials: Zeroes and Coefficients
seo_title: Polynomials Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 2)
standard_text: Zeros of a polynomial; relationship between zeros and coefficients of quadratic polynomials (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Polynomials worksheet (NCERT Chapter 2): zeroes from graphs, zeroes of quadratics, sum and product of zeroes, forming polynomials and α, β expressions. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: For ax² + bx + c with zeroes α and β.
body_html:
How it works

A zero of p(x) is a value of x with p(x) = 0. On the graph of y = p(x), the zeroes are where the graph meets the x-axis.

A polynomial of degree n has at most n zeroes.

For ax² + bx + c with zeroes α and β: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a.

A quadratic with given zeroes: x² − (sum of zeroes)x + (product of zeroes).

Example

Find the zeroes of x² − 2x − 8 and check the relationship.

x² − 2x − 8 = (x − 4)(x + 2)

Zeroes 4 and −2

Sum 2 = −(−2)/1, product −8 = −8/1

Answer: 4 and −2

Example

Find a quadratic polynomial with sum of zeroes 1/4 and product −1.

x² − ¼x − 1

Multiply by 4

Answer: 4x² − x − 4

Common mistakes

  • Writing α + β = b/a. The sign changes: α + β = −b/a.
  • Counting the turning points of a graph instead of the points on the x-axis.
  • Using α² + β² = (α + β)². It is (α + β)² − 2αβ.

faq.q: What are the zeroes of a polynomial?
faq.a: The values of x that make p(x) = 0. Geometrically, they are the x-coordinates where the graph of y = p(x) meets the x-axis.

faq.q: What is the relationship between the zeroes and coefficients of a quadratic polynomial?
faq.a: For ax² + bx + c, sum of zeroes = −b/a and product of zeroes = c/a.

faq.q: How do I find a quadratic polynomial from the sum and product of its zeroes?
faq.a: Use x² − (sum)x + (product), then multiply by a number to clear fractions if needed.

faq.q: How many zeroes can a cubic polynomial have?
faq.a: At most 3. Its graph meets the x-axis at 1, 2 or 3 points.
